summary.headline: Greaves Cotton Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 44% YoY to INR1,176 crore, but Core EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% from 14.8% on input-cost pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 44% YoY to INR1,176 crore in Q2 FY27 and 38% to INR2,150 crore in H1, with Core Businesses up 24% in Q2. Consolidated EBITDA margin improved marginally to 6.2% from 5.8% in Q1, but Core EBITDA margin contracted to 11.5% from 14.8% a year ago as commodity inflation outpaced pricing actions. Greaves Electric Mobility (GEML) posted record volumes and revenue of INR410 crore (up 106%), with its loss narrowing to INR25 crore from INR42 crore, and Excel Controlinkage became wholly owned after the 20% stake buyout. Q2 also carried INR60.1 crore of one-off charges (INR27.3 crore accelerated depreciation and INR32.8 crore exceptional items), which management says completes the write-off exercise.

financial_highlights.change: from 5.8% in Q1 FY27; EBITDA up 43% YoY in Q2
narrowed from INR42 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: INR60.1 crore (INR27.3 crore accelerated depreciation + INR32.8 crore exceptional)
financial_highlights.change: linked to GEML brands, goodwill impairment and planned GEML IPO

segments.name: Energy Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 36% YoY in Q2 (vs 21% in Q1); medium horsepower genset portfolio (160-750 kVA) grew 35% in H1 vs 28% for the segment. First batch of enhanced gensets shipped to a Middle East market.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions - Automotive Engines
segments.commentary: Grew 37% YoY in Q2, driven by three-wheeler and four-wheeler demand; launched a new 470 cc diesel engine for three-wheelers.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions - Engineered Components (Excel Controlinkage)
segments.commentary: Grew 30% YoY in Q2 on new product orders and customer wins; acquired the remaining 20% stake for INR112 crore, making it wholly owned. Overall Mobility Solutions grew 23% YoY in Q2 vs 18% in Q1.

segments.name: Industrial Solutions
segments.commentary: Reported revenue broadly flat YoY in Q2 due to exit from farm equipment; 9% like-for-like growth. Launched a 750 HP fire fighting engine and unveiled a 160 cc gasoline engine prototype.

segments.name: Greaves Electric Mobility (GEML)
segments.commentary: E-two-wheeler volumes above 37,000 units (+114% YoY); L5 three-wheeler about 2,800 units (+61%). Two-wheeler revenue INR350 crore (+134%); realisation up INR5,000 to about INR93,000 per unit; EBITDA loss per unit down about 70% to under INR6,300; EBITDA margin about -7% vs -24% a year ago.

guidance_outlook: Management says profitability is the key H2 priority; margin improvement has been slower than anticipated because commodity costs keep rising.
Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 13-15% from GREAVES.NEXT is reiterated on a mid-to-long-term basis; CFO expects H2 margins to be better than H1.
Automotive price pass-through via indexed multi-year contracts starts from Q4 FY27; Energy and Industrial price increases (enacted end-Q1) expected to flow through in Q3 and Q4.
Company-wide pricing benefit expected to be fully reflected by Q4 FY27.

GEML expects breakeven significantly ahead of earlier plan; no exact timeline given. Rights issue (INR331 crore from Greaves; INR530 crore total at GEML) expected to fund cash burn and capex for 12-18 months, with no further funding needed in that period.
Rare-earth-free ferrite-assisted synchronous reluctance motor to be deployed in two- and three-wheelers over the next quarter or two, with new product introductions in Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: GEML capacity is about 40,000 units per month with utilisation at about 40%; management expects this to cover demand for the next couple of years.
GEML is constrained by partner ecosystem and supply, not demand; management is expanding the partner ecosystem, with no numerical target given.
In H1 FY27 GEML issued LOIs for 160 new dealerships and existing dealers opened about 20 new branches.
Greaves received INR331 crore of GEML rights issue (INR530 crore total at GEML level).
Excel Controlinkage automation investment is ongoing to support its growth.
Middle East entity set up for sales and service of gensets; Greaves is building data-centre-related capability through internal development and a strategic partnership.
demand_pricing: GEML two-wheeler dealer throughput up about 40% YoY, from 18 to 25 units per month; B2B volumes up 18% in H1; e-commerce volume growth about 3x YoY.
GEML e-two-wheeler market share 4.8% in H1 FY27 vs 4.1% in H1 FY26; top two in Tamil Nadu (about 15%) and number one in Bihar (about 18%).
Management says the company is raising prices in GEML parts; GEML realisation rose INR5,000 to about INR93,000 per unit, with IoT and accessories adding higher-margin revenue.
Core commodity pressure cited on aluminium, iron, copper, and platinum group metals used in engines and gensets.

Automotive exports described as flat in H1 (not declining); domestic three-wheeler and heavy commercial vehicle demand grew faster. A French OEM is the largest engine export customer, with some further engine discussions at advanced stages.
Fire fighting engines: management is in advanced discussions with global customers after obtaining FM/UL certification, which few peers hold.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top commodity pressures and what is steady-state gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO named aluminium, iron, copper and PGM as the main cost buckets for engines and gensets. He reiterated the 13-15% EBITDA margin steady-state target and said H2 should be better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Are the e-two-wheeler loss-per-unit gains sustainable, or are there abnormal items?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said loss per unit has been falling sharply quarter on quarter through pricing, product and market-penetration strategy, and expects that trajectory to continue barring force majeure.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GEML not pushing harder on sales given industry supply shortage and low utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand exceeds supply and capacity expansion is needed; the constraint is the partner ecosystem, with no forward volume or capacity numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Has the write-off and portfolio-review exercise finished?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all key portfolio decisions are taken, Q2 accelerated depreciation and exceptional items (INR60.1 crore) cover the GEML review, and nothing more is planned, though periodic reviews will continue.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash does the company have and is a GEML IPO or spin-off planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Core cash is about INR150 crore against INR40 crore debt (net INR110 crore), with AA- rating and almost nil debt. No IPO date was given; an IPO committee is evaluating timing and the spin-off question is for that committee.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2-wheeler motor and Excel 100% ownership change the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas said the rare-earth-free motor beats the rare-earth motor on performance and costs less, and will be in production in one to two quarters. Parag said Excel is being upgraded, with 30% growth in Q2.

risks_watch: Core EBITDA margin (11.5% in Q2 vs 14.8% a year ago) depends on whether the lagged price pass-through in Q3 and Q4 offsets commodity inflation.
GEML breakeven timing is not fixed; it depends on continued volume growth and unit economics, and management declined to give a date.
GEML IPO timing and structure are undecided; an analyst's spin-off suggestion was not addressed directly.
Management said Industrial Solutions has an export opportunity in fire fighting, but no quantified order book was disclosed.
Exports in Mobility Solutions are described as flat, not growing, and the French OEM is the main engine customer.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and top-line momentum, notably GEML and Energy Solutions, but candid that margins are under pressure and recovery has been slower than planned. Management was evasive on GEML capacity expansion numbers, IPO timing and forward volumes, and on whether write-offs are fully over.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 has been another quarter of strong business momentum and we see continued progress in the execution of our strategy named GREAVES.NEXT.
While our growth momentum remains strong, profitability continued to face pressure from rising input costs.

We believe all the key portfolio decisions that were to be taken for this stage of our business plan have been addressed and we can focus then on execution and making sure we continue to grow our market shares.
We sincerely believe there's nothing more at this stage for us to do. If there was any, we would have done it right now.

growth.why: Management reiterates 13-15% steady-state EBITDA margin (GREAVES.NEXT) and H2 margins better than H1, backed by indexed auto pass-through from Q4 and Energy/Industrial price hikes in Q3-Q4; GEML has 40k/month capacity at ~40% utilisation with no new capacity added, and Core revenue grew 24% in Q2, though no explicit revenue growth guidance was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterates 13-15% steady-state EBITDA margin and H2 better than H1, with Core margin at 11.5% vs 14.8% a year ago; indexed auto pass-through starts Q4 FY27 and Energy/Industrial price hikes flow through Q3-Q4, though commodity inflation has outpaced pricing so far.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: GEML capacity is about 40,000 units/month at about 40% utilisation and management expects it to cover demand for the next couple of years; no new plant or line was announced.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: GEML e-two-wheeler volumes above 37,000 units (+114% YoY), dealer throughput up about 40% to 25 units/month, market share 4.8% vs 4.1%, and Energy Solutions grew 36% in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: GEML utilisation is about 40% and existing capacity is seen as sufficient for two years; the Excel automation spend is already ongoing, and no new capex was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No explicit revenue or margin guidance was raised; management held the 13-15% steady-state margin target and gave no numerical upgrade, with margins below plan.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Core EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% from 14.8% as commodity costs (aluminium, iron, copper, PGM) keep rising, and management says margin recovery has been slower than anticipated; GEML breakeven has no fixed date.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Rare-earth-free ferrite-assisted synchronous reluctance motor to be deployed in two- and three-wheelers over the next quarter or two, with new product introductions in Q4 FY27; 470 cc three-wheeler engine and 160 cc gasoline prototype are also in the pipeline.

rows.label: Indexed auto pass-through and Energy/Industrial price hikes
rows.why: Automotive pass-through via indexed multi-year contracts starts Q4 FY27 and Energy/Industrial price increases flow through in Q3-Q4, with full company-wide benefit by Q4 FY27 against commodity inflation.

rows.label: Fire fighting engine export and Middle East genset sales
rows.why: FM/UL-certified fire fighting engines are in advanced discussions with global customers and first enhanced gensets shipped to the Middle East, but no quantified order book was disclosed.

rows.label: GEML rights issue and possible IPO
rows.why: INR530 crore total at GEML (INR331 crore from Greaves) is expected to fund cash burn and capex for 12-18 months with no further funding needed; IPO timing is undecided with an IPO committee evaluating it.

tone.note: Management was confident on GEML volumes, Energy Solutions and top-line momentum, but cautious on margins and recovery pace, and evasive on GEML capacity numbers, IPO timing and whether write-offs are fully over; analysts pushed on loss-per-unit sustainability, capacity utilisation and the spin-off
